fieldValues.title: Escalation: does Composition get a display title, or do clients humanise its name? (srs#928)
fieldValues.decision_question: Should the Composition schema gain an optional display `title` beside its machine `name`, or should the standard rule that clients humanise `name`?
fieldValues.context: Problem: Composition has `name` (machine kebab-case) and `description` but no display title, so clients have nothing to show a person as the composition's name. srs-web Lenses invents text by humanising `name` ("renders-spec" shown as "Renders spec"), and different clients will differ. Why it matters: it is a claim about what the standard says (SP-05, no client invents semantics); a title is presentation, so RFC-015's test applies. Options and consequences: (A) add an optional `title` to Composition by RFC: additive, clients stop guessing, one new schema property; (B) rule that clients humanise `name`: no schema change, but display text stays client-invented and inconsistent; (C) do nothing: today's divergence continues. Recommendation: A, as an additive optional property, with `name` unchanged. Action needed: owner decides, then an RFC (Door 2, spec change) is opened; no implementation until it is accepted. Urgency: low, P2; srs-web#547 works today with humanising. Not group work: the group's mandate excludes Door 2 and new normative meaning.
fieldValues.friction: srs#928 is labelled ready and wg:third-party-ready, so the builder queue keeps surfacing it, but it asks for an RFC (new normative meaning, Door 2) and says no implementation issue follows until acceptance. The builder cannot execute it.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: A: optional Composition `title` via RFC. B: ruling that clients humanise `name`. C: do nothing.
fieldValues.key_requirements: Additive and optional; `name` stays the machine identifier; presentation stays view-owned (RFC-015 test); relation to Type/Field display labels stated; one way per goal.
fieldValues.decision_statement: Open an RFC proposing an optional display `title` on Composition (option A); name stays machine-readable.
fieldValues.rationale: Clients should not invent display text (SP-05); an optional additive property is the smallest change that gives every client the same label.
fieldValues.revisit_when: The RFC is drafted, or srs-web finds a second place needing a Composition label that humanising cannot serve.
fieldValues.next_steps: Owner rules A, B or C. On A: open the RFC via .claude/commands/rfc.md (Charter Check first), then file the implementation issues. On B: record the ruling and close srs#928. Issue labelled needs-input.
